name: Novice
knowledge: Has little or no practical knowledge yet. Can name the topic in broad terms and is beginning to see why it might matter.
skills: Cannot apply the capability reliably without direct support. May try with close guidance and makes exploratory first attempts.
behaviours: Shows curiosity and motivation to learn. Asks questions and is open to feedback without defensiveness.
learning: Needs guided introduction to what the capability is, why it matters and how it contributes to public value.
typical_roles: New starters; apprentices; colleagues new to digital, data, innovation or AI in their role; those returning after a long gap.
maturity_note: The beginning of the journey - curiosity and willingness to learn matter here. Colleagues move on quickly where the capability is part of everyday work.

name: Awareness
knowledge: Understands what the capability is and why it matters. Can recognise it in use and describe its importance in simple terms.
skills: Uses basic elements with support. Identifies simple opportunities where it could improve clarity, efficiency or service quality.
behaviours: Engages when encouraged. Tries new approaches with support and reflects on what worked.
learning: Benefits from structured learning and practice with examples tied to real work.
typical_roles: Operational delivery roles building foundation; administrators and caseworkers establishing reliable everyday practice.
maturity_note: A solid foundation - understanding why the capability matters and using basic elements reliably in familiar situations.

name: Working
knowledge: Understands core concepts and methods. Has reliable knowledge and can explain benefits in the context of their own work.
skills: Applies the capability independently in routine tasks. Adapts straightforward approaches to local needs with minimal guidance.
behaviours: Demonstrates the capability consistently in everyday work. Takes responsibility for own development and follows agreed standards.
learning: Builds capability through ongoing practice and learning; may work toward accreditation where relevant.
typical_roles: Policy officers, analysts, delivery staff and operations managers using the capability routinely; the benchmark for competent performance in most civil service roles.
maturity_note: Confident independent practice - the maturity target for most civil servants on strands they use every day. A meaningful mark of competence.

name: Practitioner
knowledge: Has detailed understanding including nuances and implications for quality and outcomes. Shares knowledge proactively with colleagues.
skills: Uses the capability independently across varied scenarios. Troubleshoots complex issues and improves local practice.
behaviours: Coaches and supports others informally. Models good practice and helps colleagues apply standards consistently.
learning: Pursues advanced learning where relevant and helps others build confidence and consistency.
typical_roles: Where informal influence begins - experienced specialists others rely on, and team coordinators or workstream leads who improve practice around them.
maturity_note: Practitioner is where the two routes become visible - you do not need both on every strand.

name: Expert
knowledge: Holds authoritative expertise with insight into strategic value and system-level implications. Recognised as a trusted source of guidance in your domain.
skills: Leads application across teams or services. Influences standards, governance or practice and drives improvement at scale.
behaviours: Shapes culture and expectations. Champions responsible practice and develops capability in others systematically.
learning: Undertakes specialist ongoing learning and uses expertise to elevate organisational capability and future practice.
typical_roles: Heads of profession, lead specialists, programme and function directors, G6+ leaders with authority to set direction, and cross-government leads.
maturity_note: Expert is one level with two valid demonstration patterns - you do not need both on every strand.
